a1.say: Let's build Caching Expensive Embedding Calls.

a1.cap: Computing a text embedding costs money and ~200 ms. Cache embeddings by input text so repeated texts are free, and provide a way to evict a single entry when the model changes.

lines: Computing a text embedding costs money and ~200 ms. Cache embeddings by input text so repeated texts are free, and provide a way to evict a single entry when the model changes.

a1.cap: @Cacheable("embeddings") checks the cache before running the method, keyed by its argument; on a miss it runs the method and stores the result.
a1.say: at Cacheable("embeddings") checks the cache before running the method, keyed by its argument; on a miss it runs the method and stores the result.

a1.cap: Caching works through a Spring proxy, so calling the method from inside the same class bypasses the cache. In production you'd back it with Caffeine or Redis and set a size or time limit.

a1.say: at Enable Caching switches on Spring's caching proxies.

a1.cap: The model client sits behind an interface, so tests can swap in a fake.
@Cacheable looks up the text in the embeddings cache; only a miss calls the model.
a1.say: at Cacheable looks up the text in the embeddings cache; only a miss calls the model.

a1.cap: The expensive remote call happens once per distinct text.
@CacheEvict removes one entry, for example after the embedding model is upgraded.
a1.say: at Cache Evict removes one entry, for example after the embedding model is upgraded.
